source.check: unopposed members are the only nominee in their ward in the News-Letter's list of nominations (page images checked for Clifton and Falls); votes from the News-Letter's results (INA OCR), checked against the Irish News for Dock; where the OCR of a vote is garbled the figure used is the one that agrees with both the printed valid votes and the printed majority

note: Annual election of one councillor in each of the 15 wards of Belfast Corporation (the member retiring in rotation), nominations Monday 5 January, poll Thursday 15 January 1931. Thirteen members were returned unopposed; Dock and Shankill were contested, and the Unionists took Dock from the Socialists (Belfast News-Letter, 6 and 16 January 1931). Unionist gain from the Socialists. Cunningham was a Senator. The Irish News prints M'Coubrey's label as Lab. Electorate from the Irish News (the News-Letter OCR reads 7,018); poll 58.85 per cent.
